avpn.sharingHowTo: On the other device, connect to this phone's hotspot, open that Wi-Fi network's settings and set Proxy to Manual with this address:
avpn.sharingNoHotspot: Turn the hotspot on to get the address for other devices. Until then, devices on the same Wi-Fi can use the address below.
avpn.sharingNoAddress: There is no hotspot and no Wi‑Fi right now. Turn on this phone’s hotspot and the address for other devices will show here.
avpn.sharingNote: Browsers and most apps go through the VPN this way; apps that ignore the system proxy (some games) go direct.
avpn.connectToSeeServers: Connect to see the servers and their ping
avpn.autoBestHint: Picks the server with the lowest ping
avpn.balanceHint: Spreads traffic over the fastest servers
avpn.pingTimeoutMsg: A server that doesn't answer in this time counts as unreachable
avpn.homeWifiHint: Pause the VPN on a network whose router runs one
avpn.homeWifiPauseMsg: On a home Wi-Fi the VPN pauses (the router already runs one) and comes back by itself when you leave that network
avpn.homeWifiAdd: Add this network as a home
avpn.homeWifiNotOnWifi: Connect to the home Wi-Fi and try again
avpn.homeWifiNoPanel: No VPN panel found on router $gateway (ports 3058, 9090, 9091, 9999, 7890): such a network can't be told from another
avpn.homeWifiHow: A home is told by its router, with no location access: the router's address on the Wi-Fi and its VPN panel's ports. Connect to the home Wi-Fi and tap Add. For a second home, do the same on its network.
avpn.sitesHomeMsg: The switch on the right shows the app on the home screen in the Delay block (up to $n). Drag to set the order: the handle on the right, or a long press on a row
avpn.sitesHomeLimit: The home screen shows at most $n apps
avpn.sitesHomeEmpty: Turn apps on in Settings → Sites
avpn.pingMethodMsg: HTTPS: with the encryption handshake, closer to how sites open, a higher ping. HTTP: just the server's answer, a lower ping.
avpn.pingTargetMsg: Where every server sends its test request. If the servers stop answering while the internet works, try another address.
avpn.pingTestTargetsMsg: Measure each address through the VPN: which answers, and how fast
avpn.pingNeedVpn: Turn the VPN on to test the addresses
avpn.pingAutoSwitch: Switch the address when nothing answers
avpn.pingAutoSwitchMsg: When no server has answered its ping for a minute, the next address on the list is taken
avpn.siteGroups: A server of its own for sites
avpn.siteGroupsMsg: Only the apps in the list below get a server of their own: each goes through the server steadily answering it soonest (3 tests in a row answered, chosen by their average); until there is one, through the main server. For the first minute after the VPN comes up, the network changes or an auto pause ends, the main server too, then a test every 2 minutes, only while the app is used. Open connections aren't cut. Wi-Fi and LTE each have their own settings
avpn.siteGroupsToleranceMsg: A site moves to another server only when that one answers at least this much sooner
avpn.siteGroupApps: Apps with a server of their own
avpn.siteGroupAppsMsg: Only these apps get a server of their own. Instagram, WhatsApp, Telegram, ChatGPT, YouTube and Google Drive together with their sites in any app (a browser, say), tested against their page, their flag on the home tile. The rest by the servers' ping. Remove an app and it's back on the main server
avpn.adBlockAdsMsg: Ad domains. The stricter the level, the more lists and the more sites break
avpn.adBlockMildMsg: One list (Hiddify): blocks the least, breaks sites least
avpn.adBlockNormalMsg: Two lists (Hiddify and SagerNet): the middle way
avpn.adBlockStrictMsg: Three lists: blocks the most, but breaks sites and apps more often
avpn.adBlockPhishingMsg: Scam and infected sites; it doesn't touch ordinary ones
avpn.adBlockMinersMsg: Sites that mine cryptocurrency on your device
avpn.adBlockMsg: Blocking at the VPN's level, for every app and site: the domains in the lists don't open. The three sections are switched on separately; the core downloads and keeps the lists. If a site or an app breaks, add its domain to the exceptions below
avpn.adBlockAllowMsg: A domain on this list (and its subdomains) is never blocked, in case a site or app broke. Type a site's address and press the plus
avpn.profileManagementWhitelist: Whitelist servers (БС, LTE Only) — work on the mobile network
avpn.profileManagementOrdinaryReserve: Ordinary servers — the reserve when no whitelist server is open
avpn.profileNewCountries: New countries in the profile "$profile": $countries. They are already open
avpn.profileManagementHint: Each profile's countries, with the ping to them (measured as soon as the profile is open). Ticked countries are open to the pings and to use, unticked ones are left out. Separately for Wi-Fi and LTE
avpn.profileManagementNoCountries: No server in this profile has a country I can tell
avpn.profileExtraOn: Add to the active one (servers together)
avpn.lightLookMsg: No see-through blocks or blur, no gliding animations or sliding pages, a flat background, less memory for pictures. The theme's colours stay. For a weak phone or to save battery
avpn.lightBackgroundMsg: Polls connections, ping and the screen less often while the app is out of sight: a little less CPU and memory. The look doesn't change; the sites' server choice and auto-pause react a bit slower
avpn.nightModeMsg: While the screen is locked the checks sleep: the core doesn't ping the servers, the service and the app wake less often. Everything returns with the screen. It saves noticeable battery overnight; open connections and calls aren't touched
avpn.trafficSmallHidden: No app has used 30 MB this session yet
avpn.pingSwitched: No ping for a minute — ping address now: $name
avpn.homeTrafficSmall: This session’s traffic is under 1 MB per app so far
avpn.statsPingHistory: Ping to the server, last minute
avpn.autoPauseMsg: While one of the chosen apps (a government or bank app, say) is open, the VPN turns off completely and the app can't see it. As soon as you leave it, the VPN comes back.
avpn.autoPauseNeedAccess: To know which app is open, A-VPN needs “usage access”. Turn it on for A-VPN on the screen that opens.
avpn.autoPauseHint: Turn the VPN off in chosen apps
avpn.connSearch: Search a site or an app
avpn.connNotConnected: Connect to the VPN to see which apps connect to which sites, and which way each connection goes
avpn.stTapBelow: Turn the VPN on with the button below
avpn.noAdminNote: No administrator rights: system proxy mode — browsers and most programs go through the VPN
avpn.styleContrastHint: A light top, a black bottom, white tiles; a backdrop of lines and shapes, its own palettes
avpn.styleGraphiteHint: Dark graphite and glow, a sphere button
avpn.styleClassicHint: The earlier look, cards and gradients
avpn.styleGlassHint: The same blocks and panel; a backdrop of soft colour spots, its own colour schemes
avpn.glassSchemeMsg: Glass has its own schemes: each sets the glass, the backdrop and the colour, and whether it is light or dark
avpn.topoRulesTitle: Why the traffic went that way
avpn.connectOnBoot: Turn the VPN on when the phone starts
avpn.connectOnBootMsg: The VPN comes on in the background after a restart, even if it was off before. Let the app run in the background without battery limits so the phone doesn't stop it.
avpn.autoPingOnOpenMsg: If the last check was 30 minutes ago or more, the pings refresh by themselves
avpn.statsPingPeriod: Ping to the server over the chosen period
avpn.topoRulesHint: Each rule is a list of sites or apps; on the right, where it sent their traffic
avpn.topoDayGap: The breakdown below holds $listed: connections shorter than 2 seconds and those while the app was closed aren't in it
avpn.accentOledGroupMsg: Pixels off at night: true black and one bright colour

builtinRules.bypassLanHint: The router, printer, TV and other devices at home
builtinRules.blockQuicHint: Apps switch to TCP at once, which is faster through the VPN
builtinRules.aiProxyHint: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, NotebookLM, Perplexity, Grok, DeepSeek, Copilot, Cursor… — sites and apps
builtinRules.videoProxyHint: YouTube, YouTube Music, YouTube Kids, Google TV, Twitch — apps and video
builtinRules.storesProxyHint: Google Play, F-Droid, APKPure, APKMirror, Obtainium. RuStore and Galaxy Store go direct with the Russian apps
builtinRules.foreignProxyHint: Microsoft Office, Outlook, Steam, PlayStation, Pinterest, TP-Link, MikroTik, RustDesk, Bybit, ABRP…
builtinRules.yandexDirectHint: Alice, Music, Maps, Navigator, Taxi, Disk, Mail, Eats, Lavka, Kinopoisk, Bookmate — direct

builtinRules.socialProxyHint: Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, X, TikTok, Snapchat, LinkedIn, Signal, Viber

share.where: Opens a public issue on GitHub, already filled in with these app names. To share them, submit it there. You need a GitHub account.

routing.europeOnlyServersHint: Hide servers outside Europe, including LTE Only ones. Applies on the next connect.
routing.cisOnlyServersHint: Every country of the subscription but Russia and Belarus. On mobile data the whitelist servers, also without the Russian and Belarusian ones. Applies from the next connection.
routing.serversByNetworkHint: On mobile data only LTE Only servers, on Wi-Fi only the others. Switches when the network changes.
routing.homeNetworkHint: Your WireGuard server instead of the provider: its network through it, everything else direct. Same as the Server button on the home screen.
routing.listHint: Rules are checked top to bottom: the first that fits decides where a connection goes. Drag to reorder.
routing.everythingElseVpnHint: Whatever the rules above leave goes through the VPN.
routing.everythingElseDirectHint: Only the groups above take the VPN, the rest goes direct at full speed.
routing.globalOn: "Global" is on: all traffic goes through the VPN, the rules below don't apply (except the local network and QUIC).
routing.serverOn: "Server" is on: the home network through your WireGuard, the rest direct. The rules below don't apply.
routing.everythingElseWhere: Switched in Settings, the "Everything else" row.
routing.everythingElseVpnSettingsHint: Whatever the routing rules don't cover goes through the VPN.
routing.everythingElseDirectSettingsHint: Only what the routing rules send (blocked sites, Google, AI, social networks…) takes the VPN, the rest goes direct at full speed.
